description: Figure 6(a) is a bar chart illustrating the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined, with the caption noting that researchers from the US publish the most consistently, while other countries began producing more datasets since 2016. The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 10⁰ (1), 10¹ (10), and 10² (100). Each bar corresponds to a specific year and is colored to represent the researcher location: dark blue for the US, orange for China, green for India, red for Russia, and purple for the UK. The height of each bar indicates the number of datasets published by researchers from that location in that year. For example, the US (dark blue) consistently has the tallest bars, reaching approximately 100 datasets in 2021 and 2022, while other countries show a trend of increasing dataset production, with bars for India (green) and Russia (red) growing notably after 2016. The bars are arranged chronologically along the x-axis, and no bars are visually emphasized or annotated beyond their color-coded representation.
